title: Naming the Palladium Sunday club after Blen Blen
summary: He asked Chano Pozo for permission to use a popular tune's name.

story.theme_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band monikers
story.community_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band names

blocks.x: Ah ha. Okay. Just some little questions. You mentioned a Webb arranger by the name of something like -- was it Alex Handy? Or Alexander?
Bob Alexander, okay, fine. When did China Porso own the name of Glen ? Why did he have to go to China?

Well, I tell you, the idea was when I spoke to Rico , and that was a Latin , Rico said to me, we are -- in order to present this to the public and be able to face any kind of problem that might arise,--

For this new adventure, because the people in the Palladium, what they were reacting about is (unintelligible). Frederico tried to tell these people, in the ballroom, it ain't going to be nothing that way, because we're going to present this as a club and the people restrained, you know what I mean?
So we're going to cater to the best class
of people (unintelligible), it's going to be no problem. So he said, Mario, we need our name that means something.

So I said, well, I don't know, I don't know nothing about it. He said, how about (unintelligible)? Blem-blem was a very popular tune in that particular era. I say, well, (unintelligible). Can you go to China Borbo and ask for the permission? I said, yeah, we'll go.

So he said, so we don't have to have a problem that anybody follow through to get (unintelligible). So I went to see Chino. Said, China, I need a favor from you. Said, what is it? Name it. I said, we're going to ________ something like this, and we're going to use the Blem-blem-blem. Say, you are? (Unintelligible.)
So it was named after a (unintelligible) tune.
